items.heading: Autumn Relay Prospects
items.summary: Clive Shippen previews Belgrave's 1970 autumn road relay season, regretting the loss of the Johnstone relay and criticising the presentation of A.A.A. relay championships, and lists the fixtures from 12 September to 17 October.
items.text:
Autumn Relay Prospects

Clive Shippen reviews the forthcoming road season

Once again a popular point to point relay bites the dust. First it was the classic London to Brighton, then the well established Leyton to Southend, then the Southampton to Bournemouth and now the Johnstone event. This latest casualty was in our fixture list last year and vied with the Dudley to Bridgenorth relay for the high spot of the seven week season. As holders of the trophy we are naturally dissappointed at not having the opportunity to defend it but are even more concerned at this steady erosion of quality events from our fixture list.
To suggest that the introduction of A.A.A. Championship events over 12 stages and 6 stages are suitable compensations would raise cries of derision from those who have witnessed these events. Whilst one would not quarrel with the organisation of these races between starting gun and tape there is a great deal more that requires attention in a National Championship than the race itself. Someone should be appointed to deal solely with pre-race publicity, public relations generally and the presentation ceremony itself. It is just not good enough to search around on the day for a place to"hand over" the medals or to ask the teams to shake hands with the Mayor's sixth reserve when the medals do not turn up. It has always been difficult to get a big attendance at after-race presentations but, if the present trend continues, even the successful teams won't bother to go.
It is rumoured that the National 6-stage Relay will be held on October 10th at Southport. It is ironical that of all the events in the Autumn calendar this is the only one for which we had not received details at time of press. As it happens, Belgrave will not be sending a team in any case; and we are unlikely to be the only absentees. Unless National Championships are put on with all the publicity, presentation and trappings of a truly National occasion then the longer standing events are in danger of going the same way as the 6 stage relay.
Back to the local scene, this year's fixture list covers one of the briefest periods ever---5 weeks. The programme is as follows:-

September 12th----Surrey Co. Road Relays (S & Y), Woking Lido.
" 19th----Blackheath H. Road Relay, Hayes
" 26th----Belgrave 5¾ miles handicap (non-championship).
October 3rd----Walton A.C. Road Relay.
" 10th----Belgrave 3 miles Yacht Handicap.
" 17th----Dudley to Bridgenorth and Back Road Relay.

The opening event could see us off to the best start we have had since 1951. In that year we won the Surrey Co. Road Relay for the 4th consecutive time, yet after eighteen further attempts we have failed to record another win. This year there is much determination in the camp to put the record right---an approach which has sadly been lacking in recent years. It coincides with the running into form, just at the right time, of Kerr, Thresher, North, Major and Fairclough. With Bicourt and Hart already in fine fettle we could well be having a celebration dip in the Lido on September 12th.
With our Surrey men nicely tuned up after Woking they will be joined by our other big guns, Mann, O'Hara and O'Connor for the Blackheath Relay seven days later. This year's race had been switched to a Sunday with an 11a.m start but just before going to press we hear that the event has reverted to the normal Saturday spot. There are many arguments against a Sunday morning road relay but it would have been interesting to see how well the athletes supported it.
The following Saturday (Sept.26th) is the day on which many of our dark horses have been training to reach peak. Secret sessions and time trials ("I've only been out once a week Bill") culminate in that blue riband of the road, the "5¾". All the nervous tension and needle of an international meeting is on show, with the battles becoming more gruelling the further down the field one goes. If you can't run in this one you must at least watch it!
October opens with the Walton Relay. This is a popular event over a nice course and we usually manage to enter about five teams. For those who are striving to make our team for the main event of the Autumn season and have had no real luck so far, their final chance comes with the Yacht '3' on October 10th. This popular handicap attracts as many as sixty members and Bill Lucas's handicapping has proved so good in the past that a funnel is required at the finish to produce a correct finishing order. Don't miss this one for, whatever your standard, you could be a winner; and there are prizes for the first three.
The short season reaches it's climax on October 17th with Tipton's Dudley to Bridgenorth Relay. This event attracts a top class field and we have done very well the last two years in finishing second both times-----to Derby in 1968 and to City of Stoke in 1969. The programme laid on for the preceding 5 weeks should be ample for our runners to tune up nicely for this race. Gold would be nice compensation for the loss of the "Johnstone".
All members, whatever their event or standard, are asked to study the above fixtures, decide in which events they would like to run (everyone runs in the Yacht!) and notify Gordon Biscoe at 34, Pam's Way, Ewell, Surrey. Tele: 393 4433
